metadata.title: SFTC Basketball Teaching And Planning Database
metadata.description: App-facing basketball teaching, role, tactical, S&C, injury, macro-planning, and retrieval records derived from structured basketball research drafts.

sport_profiles.planning_summary: Basketball is a high-frequency court sport with repeated accelerations, abrupt decelerations, lateral defense, jumps and landings, contact, shooting volume, tactical decision-making, and dense competition/training exposure.
training_priorities: lateral movement and defensive stance capacity
repeated sprint ability and aerobic support
shooting, handling, finishing, and passing under fatigue
role-specific screen, rebound, and contact tolerance
key_physical_qualities: Repeated Sprint and Aerobic Recovery Demand

advanced.jump_load: individualized by minutes, role, and schedule

common_injury_or_load_risks: Patellar and Quad Tendon Load Rule
ACL and Knee Control Risk Rule
Shoulder, Wrist, and Finger Risk Rule
Fatigue and Congested Schedule Risk Rule
Youth Growth and Overuse Risk Rule
Patellar Tendon And Anterior Knee Load
do_not_pair: new high-volume jump training with dense court scrimmage load
hard reactive COD work with knee, ankle, or groin symptoms
heavy lower-body eccentric work within 24 hours of important games
large shooting-volume spike with wrist, shoulder, or elbow symptoms
high-contact rebounding/screening drills during acute back or head symptoms
progression_guardrails: progress jump volume and jump intensity separately
use 24-hour knee, ankle, and tendon response before adding more plyometric or court load
build stop, pivot, closeout, and landing quality before high-speed live play
dose S&C around game schedule and player minutes
separate starters, rotation players, and low-minute players when adjusting loads

source_refs.title: Medical Resource for Basketball Team Physicians
source_refs.notes: Used for basketball-specific medical priorities, including ankle injury prevention, knee sprains, chronic back pain, overuse tendon and bone injuries, concussion awareness, team-physician medical fitness, and competition medical support.

source_refs.title: Information for Medical Staff
source_refs.notes: Used for the official FIBA framing that basketball medical staff commonly encounter ankle and knee sprains, chronic back pain, overuse tendon and bone injuries, and must manage concussion under contemporary guidance.

source_refs.title: Youth Basketball Guidelines

source_refs.title: NBA, USA Basketball Announce First-Ever Youth Basketball Guidelines
source_refs.organization_or_author: Jr. NBA, NBA, and USA Basketball
source_refs.notes: Used as an official cross-check for youth rest, adequate sleep, yearly time away, delay of single-sport specialization, and age-appropriate participation limits.

source_refs.title: USA Basketball Youth Development Guidebook
source_refs.notes: Used for progressive youth player development and for keeping S&C prescriptions aligned with age, skill development, enjoyment, and long-term participation.

source_refs.title: NBA Board of Governors Approves New Player Participation Policy
source_refs.notes: Used to separate professional availability policy from medical load management: healthy-player rest decisions have policy constraints, while injury, rehabilitation, and medical fitness remain distinct.

source_refs.title: NCAA Injury Surveillance Program
source_refs.notes: Used for the principle that collegiate basketball safety planning should be informed by ongoing injury and illness surveillance, not only coach perception.

source_refs.title: Epidemiology of Injuries in National Collegiate Athletic Association Women's Basketball: 2014-2015 Through 2018-2019
source_refs.notes: Used for collegiate women's basketball injury patterning, including higher competition injury rates, preseason risk, ankle ligament injuries, concussions, and ACL tears.

source_refs.title: 10-Year Epidemiology of Ankle Injuries in Men's and Women's Collegiate Basketball
source_refs.organization_or_author: NCAA basketball ankle injury epidemiology researchers
source_refs.notes: Used for ankle-injury timing and mechanism context, including preseason, contact-related episodes, conservative management, and prevention implications.

source_refs.title: Sports Injuries in Basketball Players: A Systematic Review
source_refs.notes: Used as a broad basketball injury pattern cross-check: ankle and knee injury prevalence, overuse concerns, and the need for prevention programming.

source_refs.title: The Relationship between Training Load and Injury Risk in Basketball
source_refs.organization_or_author: Basketball training load and injury risk review authors
source_refs.notes: Used for workload-injury relationship logic, including the need to interpret internal and external load together and avoid simplistic single-metric risk prediction.

source_refs.title: Training Load and Match-Play Demands in Basketball Based on Competition Level: A Systematic Review
source_refs.organization_or_author: Russell, McLean, Impellizzeri, Strack, and Coutts
source_refs.notes: Used for competition-level differences, intermittent high-intensity demands, position/context variation, and the need to match training to match-play demands.

planning_rules.rule: Ankle Sprain Risk Rule prior ankle sprain ankle swelling instability landing in traffic pain with cutting preseason spike Reduce chaotic jumping and cutting, add balance/proprioception/calf work, check bracing or taping plan if appropriate, and require hop and sport-specific progression before full return.
recommended_action: Reduce chaotic jumping and cutting, add balance/proprioception/calf work, check bracing or taping plan if appropriate, and require hop and sport-specific progression before full return.
